movement.title: Keys that must move when you add one server
movement.alt: The share of 100,000 keys that change server when one server is added, for clusters of 2 to 16 servers. With hash modulo N the share stays between 66 and 94 percent. With a hash ring it falls to one share in N plus 1.

evenness.title: How uneven is a ring of five servers?
evenness.alt: How far above its fair share the busiest of five servers is, as the number of points each server has on the ring grows from 1 to 256. With one point the busiest server holds far more than its share, and with hundreds of points it's close to fair.

x.label: points per server on the ring

shard-routing.title: Hashing a key to a server, in SQL
shard-routing.hint: One Postgres can't be three servers, but the arithmetic is the same. Try changing the 3 to a 4 and see how many keys get a new server.
shard-routing.setup: CREATE TABLE keys AS SELECT 'key-' || g AS k FROM generate_series(1, 10000) g;
shard-routing.query:
SELECT abs(hashtext(k)) % 3 AS server, count(*)
FROM keys GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

presets.label: Keys that move, 3 to 4
presets.sql:
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE abs(hashtext(k)) % 3 <> abs(hashtext(k)) % 4) AS moved, count(*) AS total
FROM keys;

presets.label: Postgres hash partitions
